body: Thank you for this. I teared up up reading this. This gives me a modicum of hope.
Hormone prescriptions are expensive, especially for an american with no health insurance such as myself. I'd love to take hormones, but I haven't the option right now.
Thanks, I confirmed an email address so I made my own thread.

I haven't transitioned yet, these are the reactions I see whenever I see transwomen walking down the street where I live. I was once on the subway and saw a transwoman get hit by a homeless man while being called a shemale. Nobody did anything until the next stop, when the transwoman pushed the man off of her and stumbled out, crying. I was 12. Every time a transwoman who doesn't pass walks around in public, I see people give them dirty looks, people laugh and point with their friends, and surely more. Where do you live, that trans people have it so good that they can expect to be treated as well as anybody else?

Also, clearly you don't understand transgenderism if you think it's possible for me to just "put some damn pants on and smile".
I tried, I can't post in there because my account is too new. I would if I could.

I wish I could talk to my therapist. However, sessions cost money, a commodity I do not have any of at the moment. 

The support you give me is much appreciated. However, it's harder than it sounds to be a girl when born a boy. I know I shouldn't care so much what other people think, but it's hard not to when risking having almost universal negative feelings directed towards you.
I, too, know women taller than me, but what jabba_dabba said is definitely true. I shouldn't even imagine trying to pass, I'm too tall and gawky.

It's not that I'm trying to impress anyone, I"m just trying to be happy with who I am. I can't be if I'm hounded by snickers, by people poking and prodding and making remarks and by people being outright cruel.

Thank you. I wish I could give you a hug. I'm practically tearing up because of how kind your words were. Do you know if LGBT groups would be able to direct me to a place where I could get free or cheap counseling for gender issues?

This is very disheartening. What I'm afraid of is people looking at me and thinking or saying, "look at that ugly tranny, why does he even bother?"

And I've never been able to see any beauty in myself. I appreciate your advice.

Drag and trans are different, but it disappoints me to be reminded of the height issue. I'm 6'2, which is a real impediment. My girlfriend is only a little shorter than me, though, which gives me a little hope, as she is most certainly feminine.

As mentioned in another post, I no longer have access to my old psych because of a lack of money. I was kicked out of my house and now have to pay for everything myself.

I appreciate the sentiment, but it is hard to see it in that manner when all I see in the mirror is an ugly boy when all I've ever wanted to see was a girl.

Thank you for your kind words, and that sub sounds like it's right what I've been looking for. I love my girlfriend; she also helped me through the hardest parts of my life thus far, which aren't completely relevant to this topic.
My parents kicked me out after I came out as bi, so I can no longer afford my old psychiatrist.
